name: Portable neutron spectrometer
analog: NSS, passive (Resource Prospector); depth from DAN (Curiosity)
source: NASA: DAN detects water down to about 60 cm; NSS 1.6 kg, 1.5 W (NTRS 20170010372, 20160005014)
notes: Measures hydrogen; ice is inferred. Reach is gradual (~0.4-1 m), modelled as a soft bound in the GP. Time is an assumption.

name: Ground-penetrating radar
source: RIMFAX (Hamran et al. 2020): >= 10 m depth requirement; vertical resolution 10-20 cm shallow mode, 20-40 cm deep mode; 1.245 + 2.21 kg without cables
notes: Measures the depth of a reflector, not ice: the GP treats a reflector as ice with a chance of being something else. time_min is the setup overhead (mode traverse). Hand-towed version is an assumption.

name: Powered hand core drill
analog: Apollo Lunar Surface Drill (ALSD): powered, battery, two crew (Apollo 15-17)
source: ALSD manual MCR-69-300 (< 13.6 kg; 2-3 m in dry lunar regolith); depth and time here are assumptions
notes: No EVA has drilled ice. 40 min is plausible without ice cementation, unsupported with it. ice_purity needs the core analysed after return.

name: Handheld camera / spectrometer
source: Handheld Vis-NIR and XRF ~2.5 kg each (Sehlke et al. 2019, BASALT); time is an assumption
